_game: Rush Hour (puzzle: slide cars to free the red car)
_note: Setup: (1) pip install 'git+https://github.com/chrplr/Rush-Hour.git#subdirectory=python'; (2) clone the repo to vendor/rush-hour-src and build the Go engine: `git clone https://github.com/chrplr/Rush-Hour vendor/rush-hour-src && cd vendor/rush-hour-src && go build -o rushhour-env ./cmd/rushhour-env` (the adapter auto-finds it there, or set RUSHHOUR_ENV_BIN / the phase 'binary'). Env ids: RushHour-v0, RushHour-Easy-v0, RushHourFixed-v0.
_keys_note: Env Discrete(32) is action=slot*2+direction (0=left/up, 1=right/down); slot 0 is always the red car. Humans do not press those indices: curriculum 'keys' are the adapter's meta-actions (same as rushinput.DefaultMap) — 0..3=select up/down/left/right, 4/5=select prev/next, 6/7=move back/forward. Select does not call env.step; moves become Discrete and are logged as env_action (-1 for UI-only selects). Keep the message Controls text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_ergonomics_note: White triangles on the selected car show which of its two slides are legal (from the engine action_mask), because a refused move renders identically to a dropped keypress. 'movable_only': true additionally makes 3/4 and the arrows skip cars that cannot move at all. That is NOT Rush-Hour behaviour -- its Board.Cycle/Neighbour walk every car -- and it removes the 'notice this car is stuck' part of the search, so set it to false for a design that compares fmri-gym runs against Rush-Hour runs.
